Backman is an extremely popular blogger who blogged about his wedding preparations and his experiences with fatherhood. Backman kept a personal blog and recorded various experiences in it and shared some of his writing as well. One piece of writing that became very popular with his readers was this character, which ultimately developed into Ove, the main character in A Man Called Ove . His readers encouraged him to weave the character into a book, and this is when Backman seriously started to write. He has since released two more books, both of which have done well. His first and most famous book is also going to be made into a movie. It has also been developed into a play and is popular in Stockholm. Backman is working on several new projects but doesn’t have any writing routine as such. He writes whenever he gets the time and enjoys it. Backman is married and lives with his wife and children, juggling his writing career with being a stay-at-home dad. Discussion Questions question 1 Much of the humor of the book stems from Ove’s failed attempts to kill himself. He tries many different methods to commit suicide but manages to either botch it up or someone unwittingly stops him. Do you think Ove really wanted to commit suicide at all? Give reasons for your answer. question 2 Ove is a grumpy old man who had been grumpy even before his wife died. Why do you think he was so anti-social and hated the people around him, even when he had the capacity to do good things for them? question 3 Ove has a fanatic burning hatred for bureaucrats, the people he calls the ‘men in white shirts.' Do you think he is justified in this hatred of people who are just doing their job? Why or why not? question 4 Ove’s hatred for bureaucrats is very strong because he feels powerless against them. Do you think these bureaucrats are a different sort of people altogether or are victims of the system, just like Ove himself? Give reasons for your answer. question 5 Ove always made the daily rounds in the morning to make sure everything in the neighborhood was just as it ought to be. How much value do you think this inspection had for the residents in the long run? question 6 At one point, Ove is described as a man of black and white while Sonja is all color. What did this indicate about their personalities? Do you agree with this assessment? question 8 Ove’s father was an upright man who taught him how to live an honest life and be kind to people. He also taught Ove that ‘right has to be right.’ Do you think this statement true in general? Is the same path right for everyone or does it vary according to circumstances, and why? question 9 Ove and Rune had a silly fight over which model of car they drove. The fight lasted for years. In what ways do you think Rune and Ove resembled each other? question 10 Parwaneh showed up out of the blue as Ove’s neighbor and began to pester him to do things. How much of it was because of her exuberant nature and how much because she realized the truth of Ove’s life and wanted to help him? question 11 Ove was handy and could deal with all kind of repairs, but he considers that these skills have no value these days. Do you think this is true? Why or why not? question 12 Ove had never been encouraged to show emotion and could never show love or friendship to the people around him. What influenced him to behave this way? Is this normal for the men of his generation or do you think Ove may have a personality disorder? question 13 Sonja’s father and Ove are both rude men, stuck in their own worldview. Do you think Sonja picked Ove because he was just like her father? What could she possibly have seen in Ove in their short acquaintance before they got married? question 14 Ove is very politically incorrect and rude when he talks about homosexuals. However, he is the one to help the gay boy when he needed help. What does this say about Ove’s character? question 18 Saabs United posted a positive review of this book on their website, simply because ‘Saab’ showed up around 120 times in the book. Do you think this served as a good advertisement for the brand? Why, or why not? question 19 The Independent reviewer, Lucy Scholes, says that the book proves that community spirit and social responsibility are not as lacking in current times as we think. What do you think this implies? question 20 Concorde has picked up the feature rights to the book in Germany. What is the appeal of this book to be seen in a movie?
